angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 25,804,209 km at 111.98 pc = 3.08 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 93085: distance 111.982 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.059), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 111.982 +/- 6.607 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 8.4092 +/- 0.1972 mas (same row, RUWE 1.58), 42.6 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 37.091 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 93085: radius 37.091 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 573.93 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.08) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 25,804,209 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 4642 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 93085: effective temperature 4642 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.041) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 93085: effective temperature 4642 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.041) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (Pulkovo spectrophotometric catalogue, table 5 (320-1080 nm, 2.5 nm steps, 10 nm resolution, absolute flux in W m^-2 m^-1)) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.

surfaceGravitySource: log g 2.01 from 2024A&A...683A.125P; the 6 published values span log g 2.01 to 2.4, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.2% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A%26A...683A.125P)
